statement_in_thesis: Compound loss Exp D improves +120m Pointwise CSI from 0.0796 to 0.1685 (2.12x) on validation.

statement_in_thesis: Compound loss Exp D improves +120m Circular FSS (30 km) from 0.3232 to 0.5560 (+72.0%) on validation.
mandatory_caveats_and_wording_rules: REMOVE operational utility threshold claim. 0.5 + f0/2 ~ 0.52 is a literature heuristic (Roberts & Lean 2008), not a pre-registered operational requirement. Report purely as measured comparative gain.

statement_in_thesis: On 3-day confirmatory benchmark, +180m CSI improves from 0.0120 to 0.1300 (10.8x) and FSS (30 km) from 0.0527 to 0.4333 (8.2x).
mandatory_caveats_and_wording_rules: Must explicitly disclose that July 12-14, 2023 is a locked historical benchmark previously examined in Phase 2/3, not a pristine blind test. Note chronological non-inversion.

statement_in_thesis: Compound loss Exp D achieves no statistically significant difference in bulk QPF RMSE compared to baseline Exp A at +180m.
mandatory_caveats_and_wording_rules: DO NOT state 'proves no increase in error' or 'proves equivalence'. State 'no statistically significant difference was detected (p >= 0.40)'. True statistical equivalence requires a pre-defined equivalence margin.

statement_in_thesis: At +360m, Exp D restores non-zero convective cells over baseline extinction, but absolute predictive skill remains very low.
mandatory_caveats_and_wording_rules: Never describe +360m as operationally reliable. State clearly that FSS ~ 0.05 represents very weak absolute skill; 6-hour convective forecasting remains an unsolved challenge.

statement_in_thesis: Exp D retains +180m forecast domain maximum rain rate of 13.15 mm/hr vs baseline 7.06 mm/hr on validation.
reconciled_numerical_value: Obs Max: 48.58 mm/hr, ExpA Max: 7.06 mm/hr (p99: 3.05), ExpD Max: 13.15 mm/hr (p99: 6.17)
mandatory_caveats_and_wording_rules: Explicitly state that maxima are domain-wide distribution metrics indicating heavy-tail retention, NOT proof of predicting the exact location, timing, or peak of an observed storm cell.

statement_in_thesis: Peak convective core argmax displacement exhibits median of 14.9 km at +30m and 27.2 km at +60m on test, increasing to mean 109.9 km on validation and 156.6 km on test at +180m.
reconciled_numerical_value: Test +30m Med: 14.9 km; Test +60m Med: 27.2 km; Val +180m Mean: 109.9 km (Med: 73.3 km); Test +180m Mean: 156.6 km (Med: 157.1 km)
mandatory_caveats_and_wording_rules: Must disclose this is a domain-wide single-peak argmax heuristic on matched frames, NOT object-based multi-cell tracking. 100% of large-displacement frames (> 100 km) contain multiple active convective cores.

statement_in_thesis: Stationary temporal block bootstrapping (L=12 sequences = 6.0 hours) confirms paired CSI and FSS gains at +120m and +180m are statistically significant (p < 0.001).
mandatory_caveats_and_wording_rules: Report p < 0.001 (continuity-corrected bound). State clearly that significance applies to temporal episode sampling for fixed checkpoints, not generalization across random initializations.

statement_in_thesis: Convective gains replicate across all three independent random seeds (42, 123, 999) with small across-seed variance (s_delta = 0.0089 for CSI at +180m).
